assessments.reasoning: The pinned classifier associates .asddls with ABAP CDS, explaining the classification of the two samples. The claim about Dictionary objects depends on SAP’s release-specific activation documentation.

The association sample gives a DEFINE VIEW declaration with a separately named SQL view and an association. It illustrates the source form. The names alone cannot establish that activation occurred or created two Dictionary objects.

The parameterized sample illustrates the same DEFINE VIEW form with an SQL view name and three input parameters. Together the samples show two uses of the form in one Linguist revision. Neither records the resulting Dictionary state.

SAP’s 7.54 view reference identifies DEFINE VIEW as the declaration, ties creation of two ABAP Dictionary objects to activation of its data definition, and names each object in a separate list item. The entity represents the CDS view and relies on the CDS database view as its technical basis. The Linguist classifier and samples add file and syntax context only.

limitations: The claim covers the documented DDIC-based view form. DEFINE VIEW ENTITY, abstract CDS entities, access-control definitions and downstream database behavior have distinct evidentiary scopes.
